profile_text.body:
Meta's developer site presents the company as a provider of AI models and tools for developers, offering access to Muse Spark through Muse Code and the Meta Model API. The company describes Muse Spark as tuned for long-horizon coding workflows, with fewer unnecessary turns and cleaner output, and says it performs competitively with frontier models across several coding evaluations. The site advertises a quick start that gets a first working request in under five minutes by pointing an existing OpenAI SDK compatible client at the Meta Model API, and a search grounding tool that gives a model live access to the web through a single added tool.

The company's tracked product is Llama (Meta), described as an open-weight model family that is often self-hosted. Meta is a public company, ticker META, founded in 2004 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with CIK 0001326801. Its most recent revenue filing in the record is a 10-K for the period ending 2025-12-31, reporting revenue of $200,966,000,000.

The record also lists three lawsuits involving Meta Platforms: Neural AI, LLC v. Meta Platforms, Inc. in the District Court for the Western District of Texas; Chicken Soup for the Soul, LLC v. Meta Platforms Inc. in the Northern District of California; and Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc. in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. California is listed as the jurisdiction with the largest law exposure count at 281. Several MCP servers are listed under Meta, including Meta Ads servers such as ai.adweave/meta-ads-mcp, described as having 47 tools for campaigns, creatives, audiences, and insights, co.pipeboard/meta-ads-mcp for Facebook and Meta Ads automation, and com.adbloop/meta-ads for bulk-creating Facebook and Instagram ads across accounts. The list also includes ai.fastmetal/fastmetal, ai.livingmeta/ai-in-research, ai.primeta/primeta, and app.metadock/metadock.
